source.description:
## PROBLEM
Orchestrators (agent panes) detect specialist completion via `specialists ps --json` status. For keep-alive specialists this is unreliable: a finished executor sits in status=waiting indefinitely, so status-based watchers never fire and time out (real case: darth-feedor py_backend-b2gw epic, 2026-08-23/24 — multiple 80-cycle watchers missed ecaa52/190f6a completions; detection fell back to manual feed greps).

The authoritative signals already exist but are undiscovered:
1. Project observability SQLite (`<repo>/.specialists/db/observability.db`, table specialist_jobs: status running/waiting/done/failed + updated_at_ms) — zero-byte global ~/.specialists/observability.db is a red herring.
2. Feed terminal marker `status=COMPLETE exit=agent_end`.
3. `sp log -f --json --job <id>` already streams lifecycle/control rows incl. DONE events, but its help does not present it as THE completion-detection surface.

## SUCCESS (pick scope during promotion)
- Minimum: ps help/output documents that waiting != done for keep-alive jobs and points to sp log -f / DB path for reliable detection.
- Better: new command, e.g. `sp await <job-id> [--timeout <s>] [--include-push <branch>]` — exits 0 when the job reaches terminal state (done/failed OR feed COMPLETE agent_end), printing final summary + last_output; designed for agent-pane watchers (single blocking process instead of jq/grep loops).
- Optional: ps --json gains terminal_reason / completed_at fields so one call suffices.

## NON_GOALS
No change to keep-alive semantics itself.

## EVIDENCE
Repro: launch any HIGH keep-alive executor with --background, let it finish; ps shows waiting indefinitely while specialist_jobs.status=done and feed shows COMPLETE exit=agent_end.
source.title: cli: document/automate reliable job-completion detection (ps 'waiting' hides finished keep-alive jobs)
